en flamme.explanation: "En flamme" means "a flame". To talk about a former love, say: "en gammel flamme" (an old flame).

en flaske.explanation: "En flaske" means "a bottle". To say what is in it, put the drink right after it, with no word for "of": "en flaske vand" (a bottle of water).

en flaskeåbner.explanation: "En flaskeåbner" means "a bottle opener". It is built from "flaske" (bottle) and "åbner" (opener). The last part "åbner" also appears in "en dåseåbner" (a can opener).

en fletning.explanation: "En fletning" means "a braid". The matching verb is "at flette" (to braid): "Hun fletter sit hår" (She braids her hair).

en flirt.explanation: "En flirt" means "a flirt". The matching verb is "at flirte" (to flirt): "De flirter hele aftenen" (They flirt all evening).

en flise.explanation: "En flise" means "a tile". To say where it goes, put the place before it: "en gulvflise" (a floor tile) and "en vægflise" (a wall tile).

en flod.explanation: "En flod" means "a river". To name one, say: "Rhinen er en flod" (The Rhine is a river). Do not mix it up with "en å" (a stream), which is smaller: "Der er en å bag huset" (There is a stream behind the house).

en flok.explanation: "En flok" means "a flock". It also means "a crowd" of people. To talk about animals together, say: "en flok får" (a flock of sheep). To talk about people together, say: "en flok børn" (a bunch of children).

en flok fugle.explanation: "En flok fugle" means "a flock of birds". After "flok", the birds are plural: "fugle" (birds), from "en fugl" (a bird). The first part "flok" (flock) also works for other groups: "en flok får" (a flock of sheep) and "en flok børn" (a bunch of children).

en flue.explanation: "En flue" means "a fly". The word also appears in "en fluesmækker" (a fly swatter).

en flybillet.explanation: "En flybillet" means "a plane ticket". It is built from "fly" (plane) and "billet" (ticket). The part "billet" also appears in "en koncertbillet" (a concert ticket).

en flygtning.explanation: "En flygtning" means "a refugee". The word comes from the verb "at flygte" (to flee). To say people fled, use it in the past: "De flygtede fra krigen" (They fled from the war).

en flygtningestrøm.explanation: "En flygtningestrøm" means "a flow of refugees". It is built from "en flygtning" (a refugee) and "en strøm" (a stream). "Strøm" also means electric current: "Strømmen er gået" (The power has gone out).

en flyrejse.explanation: "En flyrejse" means "a flight". Do not mix it up with "et fly" (a plane): "Flyet er forsinket" (The plane is delayed). A "flyrejse" is the trip: "Flyrejsen var forsinket" (The flight was delayed).

en flytning.explanation: "En flytning" means "a move", as in moving to a new home. It comes from "at flytte" (to move). To say you are moving, use the verb: "Vi flytter i næste uge" (We are moving next week).

en flyttekasse.explanation: "En flyttekasse" means "a moving box". It is built from "at flytte" (to move) and "en kasse" (a box). "Kasse" also means "checkout" in a shop: "Betal ved kassen" (Pay at the checkout).

en flyverdragt.explanation: "En flyverdragt" means "a snowsuit". The word is "flyver" (a pilot) plus "dragt" (a suit). To talk about the suit a pilot wears, use the same word: "Piloten har en flyverdragt på" (The pilot is wearing a flight suit).

en flyvetid.explanation: "En flyvetid" means "a flight time". It is built from "at flyve" (to fly) and "en tid" (a time). "En tid" also means "an appointment", as in "en tid hos lægen" (an appointment with the doctor).

en flåde.explanation: "En flåde" means "a fleet". To talk about the vehicles of a company, say: "en flåde af lastbiler" (a fleet of trucks).

en flåt.explanation: "En flåt" means "a tick", as in the biting animal. In Denmark, ticks can spread an illness called "borreliose" (Lyme disease).

en flødebolle.explanation: "En flødebolle" means "a chocolate-covered marshmallow treat". It is a classic Danish sweet. The name is built from "fløde" (cream) and "bolle" (a bun).

en fløjte.explanation: "En fløjte" means "a flute". It also means "a whistle". To talk about a referee, say: "Dommeren blæser i fløjten" (The referee blows the whistle).

en fod.explanation: "En fod" means "a foot", as in the body part. To say your feet hurt, Danish says "the feet" where English says "my feet": "Jeg har ondt i fødderne" (My feet hurt), literally "I have pain in the feet". To say you go on foot, use "til fods": "Han kom til fods" (He came on foot).

en fodboldkamp.explanation: "En fodboldkamp" means "a soccer match". It is built from "fodbold" (soccer) and "kamp" (match). The part "kamp" also appears in other sports: "en tenniskamp" (a tennis match).
